answer_1.quote: we introduce the first benchmark for Tunisian Arabic by systematically evaluating LLMs on their ability to generate responses in this dialect.
answer_1.outputs: generated responses in Tunisian Arabic to instruction prompts

answer_2.quote: we conducted both human- and LLM-based evaluations using four criteria: quality, correctness, relevance, and adherence to Tunisian Arabic.

answer_3.quote: we leveraged LLMs themselves to assess the responses in a self-evaluation framework. Following the LLM-as-a-Judge approach, we prompted the same LLMs to evaluate model responses using the same instruction-response pairs and evaluation criteria.

answer_4.quote: three authors of this paper served as annotators, collectively labeling the 900 evaluation instances.
answer_4.guideline: assessing two responses to the same prompt and determining the quality of the responses based on the evaluation criteria: Quality, Correctness, Relevance, and Tunisian Arabic Usage.
